# Presentations

## Workflow

1. Clarify audience, purpose, presentation length, venue, desired action, source material, and output format.
2. Build a coherent narrative before drafting slides: key message, evidence, sequence, and conclusion.
3. Give each slide one main point with a conclusion-led title. Use concise text, meaningful visuals, and consistent terminology.
4. Preserve factual accuracy; label estimates, dates, units, and sources. Keep citations or source notes traceable.
5. Match the requested visual style and accessibility needs. Avoid unreadably small text, color-only distinctions, and decorative clutter.
6. Review the complete deck in slide order, including layout, overflow, chart labels, notes, transitions, and source attribution; revise any weak or crowded slide.

## Boundaries

- Do not invent evidence, quotes, metrics, or image rights.
- Preserve the supplied template and brand rules unless asked to change them.
- Do not overwrite an existing presentation without explicit authorization; verify the exported file when possible.
